question.prompt: A triangle has vertices \(A(0,0)\), \(B(4,0)\), and \(C(0,3)\). What is the length of side \(BC\)?

solutions.explanation: To find \(BC\), take the magnitude of the vector from \(B\) to \(C\). Subtracting the coordinates of \(B\) from those of \(C\) gives \(\overrightarrow{BC}=(0-4,3-0)=(-4,3)\), whose magnitude is \(\sqrt{16+9}=5\). Thus \(BC=5\).
solutions.title: Length as vector magnitude
